sentences.text:
The Land Acquisition Officer Revenue ... vs Smt.Tatireddy
Showrilamma Died on 12 August, 2024
Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili

Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
Hon'Ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty
 LAAS.No.333 of 2018
Judgment:
(per Hon'ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty) Heard learned Government Pleader for Appeals appearing for the appellant.
None appears for respondents/claimants.

2. This appeal, under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, (for short 'the Act'), is filed by the Land Acquisition Officer (Revenue Divisional Officer), Khammam, aggrieved by the order and decree dated 30.12.2016 passed in L.A.O.P.No.54 of 2003 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge,
Khammam (hereinafter referred to as 'the Reference Court').
3.

The facts of the case, in brief, are that land to an extent of 260 square yards situated in Sy.No.93/2/2 of Khanapuram Haveli, Khammam District, belonging to the respondents/claimants was acquired for the purpose of widening and strengthening of Warangal-Khammam-Thallada road;
that draft notification under Section 4(1) of the Act was published on 29.12.2000; that possession of the subject land was taken on 29.11.2001; and that the Land Acquisition Officer, after conducting necessary award 2 AKS, J & LNA, J enquiry, passed Award No.18/2002, dated 22.05.2002, granting compensation of Rs.80,000/- for the acquired land.

4. The respondents/ claimants received the compensation granted by the Land Acquisition Officer under protest and sought reference under Section 18 of the Act and the same was numbered as L.A.O.P.No.54 of 2003 on the file of the Reference Court.
5. Before the Reference Court, on behalf of the respondents/claimants, P.W-1, who is one of the claimants, was examined and Exs.A-1 and A-2 were marked.

On behalf of the Referring Officer,
R.W-1 was examined and Ex.B-1-Award was marked.

6. The Reference Court by the impugned order enhanced the market value of the acquired land to Rs.275/- per square yard, apart from granting other benefits under the Act to the respondents/
claimants.
7. Aggrieved by the impugned order passed by the Reference Court, the present appeal is filed.

sentences.text: Learned Government Pleader for Appeals contended that the Reference Court erred in relying upon the exhibits marked on behalf of the respondents/claimants and thereby, erred in enhancing 3 AKS, J & LNA, J the compensation exorbitantly and therefore, he seeks to set aside the impugned order of the Reference Court.

9. In the instant case, before the Reference Court, the respondents/claimants, in support of their claim for enhancement of compensation granted by the Land Acquisition Officer, have got marked Ex.A-2-Valuation Certificate issued by the Joint Sub- Registrar, Khammam.

However, in view of the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Choda Dharampal Reddy Vs. Revenue Divisional Officer, Nalgonda District 1, that the Valuation Certificate issued by the Sub-Registrar on the basis of the Basic Valuation Register was only relevant for the purpose of the Stamp Act and that such a Valuation Certificate cannot form basis for determination of the market value under Section 23 of the Act, Ex.A-2 cannot form basis for determination of market value of the acquired land.

sentences.text:
10. It is undisputed that the subject land situated in Sy.No.93/2/2 belonging to the respondents/claimants was acquired along with other lands situated in Sy.Nos.74, 75, 88, 93, 144,
201, 202, 203, 205, 206, 207, 209 and 210 of Khanapuram Haveli, 1998(1) ALD 261 (DB) 4 AKS, J &
LNA, J Khammam Urban Mandal, for the purpose of widening and strengthening of Warangal-Khammam-Thallada road and the Land Acquisition Officer passed common Award No.18/2002 for the acquired lands along with the lands situated in Sy.Nos.202/2 and 203/2 of the same village.
The Land Acquisition Officer fixed the market value of the lands acquired in Sy.Nos.202/2 and 203/2 @ Rs.40/- per square yard.

The claimants therein received the said compensation under protest and the matter was referred to the Reference Court, vide LAOP.No.15 of 2003 and the Reference Court enhanced the compensation from Rs.40/- per square yard to Rs.275/- per square yard.

Challenging the said order, LAAS.Nos.186 of 2010 and 241 of 2011 were filed by the claimants therein and the Land Acquisition Officer, respectively, before this Court and this Court, vide common judgment, dated 09.07.2012, dismissed both the said Appeals.
The matter was carried to Hon'ble Supreme Court by way of SLP(C).No.3315 of 2014 and the Hon'ble Supreme Court by judgment, dated 31.01.2014, upheld the said common judgment rendered by this Court.
Thus, the matter attained finality.
5 AKS, J & LNA, J 12.

The village, the draft notification issued under Section 4(1) of the Act, the purpose of acquisition and the Award passed in respect of the subject acquired lands are same as that of the subject lands covered under the aforesaid common judgment dated 09.07.2012 passed in LAAS.Nos.186 of 2010 and 241 of 2011, which was upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in SLP(C).No.3315 of 2014, vide judgment dated 31.01.2014.
Therefore, the aforesaid common judgment is squarely applicable to the facts of the case.
13. In view of the common judgment dated 09.07.2012 passed by this Court in LAAS.Nos.186 of 2010 and 241 of 2011, this Appeal is liable to be dismissed.
14. Accordingly, this Appeal is dismissed.
